Keywords: Volvariella volvacea, ARTP, genome shuffling, high polysaccharide yield, extracellular polysaccharides · Volvariella volvacea (Bull.) Singer, commonly known as orchid mushroom, hemp mushroom, or Chinese mushroom, is a typical species of tropical and subtropical edible fungi [1,2]. It is primarily cultivated in Hunan, Taiwan, Guangxi, and Guangdong.
V. volvacea, a fungal species of Volvariella in the family Pluteaceae, has a distinctive aromatic profile and nutritional richness [3,5]. Polysaccharides, particularly those derived from the mycelia and fruiting bodies, constitute the predominant bioactive components of this edible fungus, demonstrating significant pharmacological properties, including antioxidant efficacy, lipid metabolism regulation, and immunomodulatory functions [49]. Current research primarily focuses on enhancing cold tolerance and postharvest preservation techniques.
Additionally, potassium and magnesium concentrations are elevated during the button stage relative to the other growth phases [5]. Notably, this species has the highest vitamin D content among edible mushrooms, significantly enhancing its nutritional value [6]. Furthermore, carbohydrates constitute 50–65% of the fruiting body’s dry mass, with a progressive increase observed during maturation [5]. The diverse nutrient profile of V. volvacea fulfills daily dietary requirements, underscoring its potential as a candidate for functional food development.
